page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine tailored with a compute-leaning resource profile. Powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, accompanied by a 260 MB L3 cache and support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets.

The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage or attached GPUs, requiring reliance on remote storage solutions. Benchmark measurements reflect strong raw execution capability, with top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core (2042.0) and multi-core (16898.0) workloads, as well as high-throughput static web serving at 55.94 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows large-block read bandwidth reaching 205.24 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 199.18 GB/sec.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the D32ls_v6 offers cost efficiency for applications that prioritize multi-threaded compute density over large memory footprints. However, workloads requiring expansive in-memory caches, attached local NVMe drives, or GPU acceleration will face constraints. It is best suited for compute-heavy web serving, parallel compilation pipelines, compression tasks, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 64.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 260 MB L3 cache, and instruction support for AMX and AVX-512. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, directing I/O to network-attached disks. Benchmarks show upper-quartile scores in multi-core processing, static web serving throughput, and large-block memory read bandwidth. With a reduced memory-to-core ratio, it offers high processing density for CPU-intensive workloads such as multi-threaded batch operations, code compilation, and web application hosting.
